# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.

# Repository Exploration Report: /app (transaction-enrichment-python)

## 1. Overall Codebase Structure

**Language:** 100% Python 3.9 (pandas/numpy vectorized regex rules; Flask web service). No other languages, no README, no config files beyond `setup.py`, `Dockerfile`, `.gitignore`. Single commit repo ("import codebase").

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                                # python:3.9.2, gunicorn on port 9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                              # deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, gunicorn, sklearn
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                       # Flask app factory + request timing hooks
        ├── Controller.py                     # HTTP routes; per-bank dispatch pipeline (936 lines)
        ├── BankScripts/                      # 35 bank-specific categorizers (HDFC.py, SBI.py, ICICI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, IDBI.py, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/                   # shared regex constants + cross-bank enrichment stages
```

**Architecture:** A Flask microservice ("categorizationapp"). The design pattern everywhere is: build a list of `[boolean pandas condition, label/extraction]` pairs and apply `np.select(...)` over a transactions DataFrame. Columns produced: `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`, `party2`, `city`, `isInternalPayment`, `isSalary`, PFM fields.

**Pipeline (per request, in `Controller.py`):**
1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df` – normalize input
2. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` – bank-specific category + partyName extraction
3. `card_clean_names` / `card_purpose` (credit cards only)
4. `purpose` – subcategory/merchantType
5. `clean_names` – merchant canonicalization
6. `internal_payment` – self-transfer detection (fuzzy match vs account holder)
7. `salary_detection` (SAVING accounts)
8. `pfm_categorization` + `simple_description` (if `isPFMEnabled`)

## 2. Transaction Categorization / Labeling Logic

**Entry point / dispatcher:**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` – routes `POST /categorizeTransaction` (payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `transactions`) and `POST /recurrentTransactions`. Giant if/elif on bank name (ANDHRA_BANK, SBI, ICICI, HDFC, IDFC, ..., YES) each running the same pipeline.

**Per-bank classifiers (where cheque/transfer/refund/reversal/mandate types are assigned):**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` – 35 files, each exposing one function `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)`. The first `conditions_choices` block assigns `transactionCategory` with labels such as `CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `CHEQUE_RETURN`, `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`, `TRANSFER` (default), `FUND_TRANSFER`, `TPT`, `UPI`, `IMPS`, `NEFT`, `RTGS`, `REFUND`, `REVERSAL`, `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`, `UPI_REVERSAL`, `IMPS_REVERSAL`, `ATM_REVERSAL`, `AUTO_PAYMENT`, `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, `ECS_PENALTY`, `TAX_REFUND`, `CASHBACK`, etc.
  - Representative examples:
    - `HDFC.py` (`categorize_HDFC_transactions`): refunds (`UPI.*REFUND|^REF-...`), card reversal (`^POS.*RVSL|^CRV POS` -> `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`), cheque (`CHQ DEP|CHQ PAID|MICR CLG` patterns), account verification (`BANK_VER` regex + amount < 2), heuristic reversal detection via matched DEBIT/CREDIT pairs (`shift(periods=1)` on lines 98-99).
    - `SBI.py`: mandate verification/charges (`^ACH MANDATE CHARGE|E mandate` -> `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES`), `CMP MANDATE|ACHDr` -> `AUTO_PAYMENT`.
    - `IDBI.py`: `\bACH-|Direct Debit|^NACH` -> `AUTO_PAYMENT`, `E mandate` -> `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES`, `REJECT:|OW CHQ|bounce` -> `CHEQUE_RETURN`.
    - Similar per-bank mandate rules in `Kotak.py` (line 39), `Canara.py` (44), `PNB.py` (14), `Central.py` (23, 52), `BOI.py` (21), `Federal.py` (21), `Syndicate.py` (34), `UnionBank.py` (30), `KarurVyasa.py` (22), `BankOfMaharashtra.py` (39), `ICICI.py` (32).

**Shared regex libraries (the actual "rules"):**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` – cross-bank keyword regexes for subcategories: `SALARY`, `LOAN_REP*`, `CREDIT_CARD`, `REFUND`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, `INSUFF_BOUNCE`, `INTERNAL_PAY`, merchant classes (SHOPPING, UTILITY, RESTAU, GAMING, ...).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` – bank-specific patterns: account/penny-drop verification (`ACC_VERIF`, `BANK_VER`, `BANK_VER_ICICI`, `BANK_VER_HD`, `ACC_VERI_*`), mandate autopay (`SBI_AUTOPAY5/6` = "CMP MANDATE DEBIT"), ECS/NACH return penalties (`ECS_PENAL*`), reversal patterns per bank (`REVERSAL_KV`, `REVERSAL_YES`, `REVERSAL_CITY`, ...), cheque patterns (`HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1-10`, `CHQ_RTN_*`), fund transfer patterns (`FT_PATTERN0-19`, `FT_CHQ_PATTERN1-37`).

**Post-categorization enrichment:**
- `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` – `purpose(transactions, accountType)`: assigns `transactionSubcategory` (SALARY, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, RENT, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE vs INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE for cheque returns, INTERNAL_PAYMENT, ...) and `merchantType`.
- `UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py` – `card_purpose(transactions)`: credit-card equivalents.
- `UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` – `pfm_categorization(transactions)`: maps to PFM categories.
- `UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` – `simple_description(transactions)`: user-facing description from the category list.
- `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` – `internal_payment(...)`: flags self/internal transfers via fuzzywuzzy match of `partyName` against `accountHolder` (sets `isInternalPayment`).
- `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` – `salary_detection(transactions)`: recurring-credit salary heuristics (uses sklearn/scipy).
- `UtilityScripts/RecurrentTxns.py` – `recurrent_transactions(transactions)`: recurring transaction grouping for `/recurrentTransactions`.
- `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` and `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` – display-name enums (e.g. `ECS="ECS/NACH"`, `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES="Auto Mandate Charges"`, `CHEQUE_RETURN="Cheque Bounce"`). Note: currently only referenced by SimpleDescription-style lists; categories in BankScripts are raw strings.

## 3. Payee / Counterparty Name Extraction

Name extraction happens in **two layers**:

**Layer 1 – token slicing inside each BankScript** (each file assigns `partyName` via a second/third `conditions_choices` block):
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` – the core string helpers used everywhere:
  - `sep_by_dash/sep_by_/sep_by_colon/sep_by_wave/sep_by_star/sep_by_comma/sep_by_under/...(description, n1, n2)` – split narration on a delimiter and take token slice [n1:n2].
  - `py_extract(description, pat, index)` – regex capture-group extraction with NaN handling.
  - `fuzzy_match(s1, s2, dist)` – fuzzywuzzy ratio.
- Your two example narrations map directly to **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py`**:
  - `"ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES"` -> line 83: `^ACH-BD-NACH` => `sep_by_dash(description, 2, 3)` (yields "NACHACME INDUSTRIES"-style slice; sibling rule line 84 `^ACH-BD-` takes token 2-3). HDFC has the analogous rule at HDFC.py line 169 (`^ACH D- BD-NACH-` -> token 3-4, digits stripped).
  - `"GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR"` -> line 110: `^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}` => `py_extract(pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)")` capturing "RAVI KUMAR". Similar IFSC-ref+name patterns exist in `StandardCharted.py` (lines 90-129, `[A-Z]{5}[0-9]+ (.*)`), `Indusind.py` (NEFT DebitINDBH[0-9]{11}...), `HDFC.py` (NEFT CR-<IFSC 11 chars>-... at lines 157-159).
- Other rich examples: `HDFC.py` lines 146-273 (UPI/IMPS/NEFT/cheque/ACH party extraction + stop-word cleanup + `party2` (whitespace-stripped copy) creation), `Kotak.py` (NACH-*-DR-* slicing, `MB:BILLPAY FOR (.*)` patterns), `PNB.py` (`PNB_CHQ_*`, `PNB_RTGS_*`, `CPH/TP ACH (.*)/`), `UnionBank.py` (`UB_NEFT_1..8`, `UB_RTGS_*`).
- Extraction regexes live centrally in `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` (NEFT_PATTERN0-7, IMPS_PATTERN1-8, RCVD_FROM_IMPS1-5, FT_PATTERN/FT_CHQ_PATTERN families, HDFC_CHQ/FT patterns, CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK / REMOVE_BANK_CB bank-name strippers, ECS_START/ECS_END trimmers).

**Layer 2 – canonicalization to clean merchant names:**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (1971 lines) – `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)`: ~1900 rules mapping raw partyName/description fragments to canonical merchants ("Airtel DTH", "BESCOM", "HDFC Bank Loan", equity/utility/lender names, incl. NACH loan descriptors at lines 602, 1747, 1756).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py` (927 lines) – `card_clean_names(transactions)`: same for credit-card statements.
- `IDBI.py` lines 142-245 also derive a `city` column from card-payment partyNames.

## 4. How to Run / Tests

**There are no tests in this repository.** No `tests/` directory, no `test_*.py` files, no pytest/tox/CI configuration, no Makefile, no README. The only verification path is running the service and exercising the HTTP API.

**Running the app:**
```bash
# Option A: Docker (as designed)
docker build -t categorizationapp /app
docker run -p 9898:9898 categorizationapp

# Option B: local
cd /app/categorizationapp
pip3 install -e .
gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# or dev mode: python -m categorizationapp  (runs Flask debug on :9898 via __init__.py __main__ guard)
```

**Manual smoke test:**
```bash
curl localhost:9898/                          # {"response": "Hello! Flask."}
curl -X POST localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "bank": "IDBI", "acc_type": "SAVING", "accountUID": "u1", "accountHolder": "Ravi Kumar",
  "isPFMEnabled": false,
  "transactions": [{"description": "ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES", "amount": 1500,
                    "type": "DEBIT", "balanceAfterTransaction": 10000, "remark": ""}]
}'
```
Required transaction fields (inferred from code): `description`, `amount`, `type` ("DEBIT"/"CREDIT"), `balanceAfterTransaction`, and `remark` (used by HDFC/IDBI cheque rules). Beware: deps are pinned old (Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4) and were built for Python 3.9.2, so use the Docker image or a matching venv. If you add tests, natural seams are the pure functions `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(df, accountType)`, `purpose(df, accountType)`, `clean_names(df, accountType, bank)`, and the `AppUtil` helpers — all take/return plain DataFrames with no I/O.

Runs the IDBI and Indusind categorizers directly (they are pure DataFrame
functions) against:
  A) the five broken shapes from the incident tickets
  B) a corpus of everyday shapes that are labeled correctly today

Usage: python3 harness.py [--expect-fixed]

(if that file exists).

import sys, json, os
sys.path.insert(0, "/app/categorizationapp")

import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.IDBI import categorize_IDBI_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Indusind import categorize_Indusind_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Axis import categorize_Axis_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions


def run(bank_fn, rows, acc_type="SAVING"):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["description", "amount", "type", "balanceAfterTransaction", "remark"])
    df["description"] = df["description"].str.strip()
    out = bank_fn(df.copy(), acc_type)
    return out


# ---------------- incident cases ----------------
def incident_results():
    res = {}

    # Case 2 + 3: IDBI names
    idbi = run(categorize_IDBI_transactions, [
        ("ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES", 55000, "CREDIT", 100000, ""),   # ticket 2: salary via NACH
        ("GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR",  12000, "CREDIT", 112000, ""),   # ticket 3: inbound transfer
    ])
    res["case2_partyName"] = idbi.iloc[0]["partyName"]
    res["case3_partyName"] = idbi.iloc[1]["partyName"]

    # Case 1: Indusind cheque, remark is just the 6-digit cheque number
    ind1 = run(categorize_Indusind_transactions, [
        ("TRANSFER TO SOME PAYEE", 25000, "DEBIT", 75000, "123456"),
    ])
    res["case1_category"] = ind1.iloc[0]["transactionCategory"]

    # Case 4: Indusind mandate token confirmation, nominal Re 1
    ind4 = run(categorize_Indusind_transactions, [
        ("SI MANDATE TOKEN CONFIRMATION", 1, "CREDIT", 75001, ""),
    ])
    res["case4_category"] = ind4.iloc[0]["transactionCategory"]

    # Case 5: Indusind card refund on SAVING account (amount >= 10)
    ind5 = run(categorize_Indusind_transactions, [
        ("POS TXN-AMAZON RETAIL", 1499, "CREDIT", 76500, ""),
    ], acc_type="SAVING")
    res["case5_category_saving"] = ind5.iloc[0]["transactionCategory"]
    return res


# ---------------- regression corpus (currently-correct rows) ----------------
def regression_results():
    out = {}

    idbi_rows = [
        # everyday IDBI shapes
        ("UPI/1234567890/Payment/somebody@okhdfc", 500, "DEBIT", 9500, ""),
        ("NEFT-IDIB000K123-JOHN DOE-SAL", 30000, "CREDIT", 39500, ""),
        ("ACH-BD-XYZ FINANCE LTD", 2500, "DEBIT", 37000, ""),         # generic ACH-BD- rule (line 84)

        ("NACH,~EMPLOYER LTD~XYZ", 40000, "CREDIT", 74900, ""),       # NACH comma rule
        ("POS/AMAZON/MUMBAI", 700, "DEBIT", 74200, ""),
        ("123456-RENT PAYMENT", 15000, "DEBIT", 59200, ""),           # cheque with 6-digits + dash
        ("CHQ Paid/123456/SOMEBODY", 5000, "DEBIT", 54200, ""),
        ("Int.Pd:SB Interest", 120, "CREDIT", 54320, ""),
        ("IMPS/P2A/123456789012/RAVI", 2000, "CREDIT", 56320, ""),
        ("account verification penny", 1, "CREDIT", 56321, ""),
        ("E mandate charges", 59, "DEBIT", 56262, ""),
        ("RTGS/UTIBH12345678901/BIG CORP/", 250000, "CREDIT", 306262, ""),
    ]
    df = run(categorize_IDBI_transactions, idbi_rows)
    out["idbi"] = df[["description", "transactionCategory", "partyName"]].to_dict("records")

    ind_rows = [
        ("UPI/pay/1234/merchant@icici", 350, "DEBIT", 9650, ""),
        ("NEFT DebitINDBH12345678901 HDFC0001234 SOME VENDOR HDFCR520", 10000, "DEBIT", 8000, ""),
        ("VISA POS TXN AT IN/BIG BAZAAR", 899, "DEBIT", 7101, ""),
        ("POS TXN-FLIPKART MID01234", 2100, "DEBIT", 5001, ""),
        ("CHEQUE PAID 998877", 4000, "DEBIT", 1001, ""),               # cheque via description keyword
        ("TRANSFER TO SOMEONE", 300, "DEBIT", 701, "54321"),           # 5-digit remark cheque (works today)
        ("POS TXN-SMALL SHOP", 5, "CREDIT", 706, ""),                  # small POS credit -> REFUND today
        ("Int.Pd Interest", 12, "CREDIT", 718, ""),
        ("IMPSP2A123456789012INDBRAVI KUMAR 99", 1500, "CREDIT", 2218, ""),
        ("ATM CASH TXN 112233", 2000, "DEBIT", 218, ""),
        ("penny drop Account Validation", 1, "DEBIT", 217, ""),        # Re1 DEBIT -> ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION
        ("MNDTVRFCHGS GST", 118, "DEBIT", 99, ""),
    ]
    df = run(categorize_Indusind_transactions, ind_rows)
    out["indusind_saving"] = df[["description", "transactionCategory", "partyName"]].to_dict("records")

    # POS TXN credit on CURRENT account (should stay whatever it is today)
    df = run(categorize_Indusind_transactions, [
        ("POS TXN-CARD SETTLEMENT MID099", 5400, "CREDIT", 10000, ""),
    ], acc_type="CURRENT")
    out["indusind_current"] = df[["description", "transactionCategory", "transactionSubcategory"]].to_dict("records")

    # Sanity: neighbours that share the mutated shapes at other banks must not move
    df = run(categorize_Axis_transactions, [
        ("NACH E MANDATE registration", 1, "DEBIT", 999, ""),
        ("TRANSFER", 100, "DEBIT", 899, "654321"),                    # Axis 6-digit remark cheque
    ])
    out["axis"] = df[["description", "transactionCategory"]].to_dict("records")

    df = run(categorize_HDFC_transactions, [
        ("ACH D- BD-NACH-EMPLOYERX-123", 50000, "CREDIT", 60000, ""),
        ("CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-123456", 7000, "DEBIT", 53000, ""),
    ])
    out["hdfc"] = df[["description", "transactionCategory", "partyName"]].to_dict("records")

    return out


def main():
    expect_fixed = "--expect-fixed" in sys.argv
    inc = incident_results()
    print("== incident cases ==")
    for k, v in inc.items():
        print(f"  {k}: {v!r}")

    expected = {
        "case1_category": "CHEQUE_PAID",
        "case2_partyName": "Acme Industries",
        "case3_partyName": "Ravi Kumar",
        "case4_category": "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION",
        "case5_category_saving": "CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL",
    }
    if expect_fixed:
        bad = {k: (inc[k], want) for k, want in expected.items() if inc[k] != want}

    reg = regression_results()
    snap_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "regression_before.json")

    else:
        with open(snap_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(reg, f, indent=1)
        print(f"snapshot written to {snap_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

steps.message:
Resolved. Five one-token regressions, all in the deterministic rule tables, each matching one ticket exactly.

## Root causes and fixes

**Ticket 1 — cheque filed as general transfer** (`Indusind.py:64`)
The remark-based cheque rule matched `^[0-9]{5}$` — exactly 5 digits — so a standard 6-digit cheque number in the note fell through to `TRANSFER`. Sibling banks (Axis, PNB, Bank of Maharashtra) all use `{5,6}`. Fixed to `^[0-9]{5,6}$`.

**Ticket 2 — salary shows payee "NACH"** (`IDBI.py:83`)
`ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` was sliced at dash-token `[2:3]`, which is the literal `NACH`. As written the rule was also byte-identical to the generic `^ACH-BD-` rule below it, i.e. dead. Fixed to `[3:4]` → `Acme Industries` (mirrors HDFC's analogous `ACH D- BD-NACH-` rule which takes token 3).

**Ticket 3 — sender name blank on `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`** (`IDBI.py:110`)
`py_extract(..., pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` asked for capture group 1 of a single-group pattern, so it always returned empty. Every legitimate `index=1` in the codebase has a two-group pattern. Fixed to `index=0` → `Ravi Kumar`.

**Ticket 4 — mandate token charge filed as transfer** (`Indusind.py:30`)
The mandate→`ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` rule required `amount == 2`; every other bank's verification rule (including the Axis rule this file mirrors) keys on the nominal ₹1. Fixed to `amount.eq(1)`.

**Ticket 5 — card refund label depends on account category** (`Indusind.py:26`)
The `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` rule compared `accountType == "SAVINGS"`, but the service only ever passes `"SAVING"` (verified across Controller.py and every other script — `"SAVINGS"` appeared nowhere else). The rule could never fire, so the next rule mislabeled these credits as plain `REFUND`. Fixed to `"SAVING"`.

## Verification

The repo has no tests, so I built a harness (`/tmp/opencode/harness.py`) that calls the categorizers directly:

- **Before:** `TRANSFER`, `Nach`, `''`, `TRANSFER`, `REFUND` — reproducing all five tickets verbatim.
- **After:** `CHEQUE_PAID`, `Acme Industries`, `Ravi Kumar`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`.
- **No collateral movement:** a 30-row corpus of currently-correct shapes (everyday UPI/NEFT/POS/cheque/verification rows for IDBI and IndusInd, plus the neighbouring Axis/HDFC rules that share the mutated patterns) was snapshotted before the fix and is byte-identical after.
- The fixed rows also survive the full Controller pipeline (`purpose` → `clean_names` → `internal_payment`) with correct final output.
